presentation.label: Apply Scene
presentation.summary: Hold SCENE A or SCENE B and press YES: that scene's locked values become the active Part's own. Hold both and press YES to keep the crossfader's current blend. In grid recording, hold trigs and press a scene key (or both) to write the same values as p-locks on those steps.
presentation.overview: Keep a scene, or keep a blend. SCENE A + YES writes every value scene A locks into the active Part, as if you had turned each knob there yourself; SCENE B + YES does the same for scene B. Hold both scene keys and press YES to write the sound the crossfader plays right now instead. The scenes, the crossfader and the saved Part stay as they were, so the scenes keep morphing from the new base and RELOAD PART takes you back to the last saved Part. In grid recording the same gesture works on steps: hold trigs, press SCENE A, SCENE B or both, and let go; the values become p-locks on the held steps of the active track.
highlights: Covers every scene-lockable page on all eight audio tracks: SRC (the assigned machine), LFO speed and depth, AMP, FX1 and FX2.
One scene: its locked values, wherever the crossfader is and even when that scene is muted.
The blend: the value stock's scene morph plays at the current crossfader position, rounded to the nearest knob step; a muted scene counts as not locked, exactly as stock morphs it.
On trigs: hold trigs in grid recording and press a scene key, or both: the scene's values, or the blend at the current fader position, become p-locks on those steps.
Nothing new is stored: the result is ordinary Part data that saves, loads and survives a power cycle like a hand-turned knob.
Pressing it when nothing would change shows NOTHING TO APPLY.
usage: Lock some parameters in SCENE A and SCENE B. Hold SCENE A (or SCENE B) and press YES to make that scene's values the Part's own: SCENE A APPLIED (or SCENE B APPLIED).
To keep an in-between sound, move the crossfader, hold SCENE A and SCENE B, and press YES: SCENE BLEND APPLIED.
Save the Part to keep it, or press FUNC + CUE (RELOAD PART) to go back to the last saved Part.
To put a scene on particular steps: in grid recording hold the trigs, press SCENE A (or SCENE B, or both for the blend) and let go: SCENE A TO TRIGS. Hold a trig and press PLAY to clear its p-locks.

limitations: YES with SCENE A, SCENE B or both held no longer shows ARM ALL; YES alone still does.

In grid recording, SCENE A or SCENE B pressed with trigs held writes p-locks when the last scene key is released. A trig pressed or a knob turned inside that gesture keeps its stock meaning (scene select, scene lock) and then nothing is written.

The crossfader stays where it is and the scenes keep their locks: a parameter locked in both scenes keeps its sound, while one locked in only one scene can change (after a one-scene apply it plays that lock at every fader position; after the blend stock blends that lock with the new base).
XVOL and XLV (the crossfader volume locks) have no Part knob and stay scene locks.
Trig locks and LFO modulation are not written into the Part; the result is the sound on steps without a trig lock.
On trigs: only the active track and the held steps of the trig page shown. There is no undo beyond stock's hold trig + PLAY, which clears all of that step's p-locks.
With MASTER TRACK on, track 8's SRC and AMP scene locks are not applied: stock has no knob there.
Not in MIDI mode, and not on MIDI tracks (stock has no scene locks there).
Undo is stock RELOAD PART, which also discards any other unsaved edits since the last Part save.

Tested on one MKII over USB: the Part apply with 0.1.0 (values watched, no audio check); TRIG + SCENE with 0.2.0, including playback by ear, a project save and a power cycle. Not tested on the MKI; the card build was not run on hardware.

storage.label: Storage
storage.display: 2,062 bytes of ColdFire code and state in the DRAM reserve; no DSP code, no saved data
storage.conditions: Assembled unit size (m68k-elf-size) of the 0.2.0 source; 636 bytes in 0.1.0.

processing.label: CPU / DSP load
processing.display: None while idle; 2.3-11.1 M ColdFire instructions per apply (emulator)
processing.conditions: ot_emu, executed instructions from the YES press to the toast: 110 to 160 parameter writes in all three modes, 201 with every scene byte locked (frame engine off), and 11.1 M for 231 writes with the frame engine on, interrupts included; no DSP work. Under a MIDI flood in ot_emu nothing changes between presses. Hardware time not measured.

impact.conditions: One apply at its dearest: the blend with every scene-lockable byte of all eight tracks locked in both scenes. Nothing runs between presses.

cpu.rationale: No idle cost. One press runs in the UI task: 2.3 to 6.3 million executed ColdFire instructions for 110 to 160 parameter changes under ot_emu, 8.3 million for the 201 changes of the worst case (11.1 million for 231 changes with the frame engine running, interrupts included), most of it stock's own store and redraw per change. Time on the unit is not measured.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code. The new Part values reach the DSP through stock's own parameter store, as a turned knob does.

memory.rationale: 2,062 bytes of ColdFire code and state (101 bytes of it state: the YES press and the TRIG + SCENE chord); no DSP memory and no saved data of its own.

tests.summary: On one MKII over USB: 0.1.0's SCENE + YES modes, NOTHING TO APPLY, Keep, Undo, removal and a power cycle (user-reported, 15 Oct); 0.2.0's TRIG + SCENE driven by the agent on a development twin (one scene, the blend at the morph model's values, repeat, stock gestures inside the chord, three trigs, muted scene, stock clear, playback lane, removal) and run by the user on the flashed base (playback by ear, project save, power cycle). Under ot_emu (verify.py, 264 checks): the Part apply as in 0.1.0, and TRIG + SCENE's locks equal the model on every held step with nothing else in the pattern moved, through project save, reload and an emulated power cycle.

conditions.parameterExtremes: SCENE + YES: every scene-lockable byte of all eight tracks locked in both selected scenes (A at each slot's minimum, B at its maximum): 201 writes for the blend at fader 64, 8,268,814 instructions on 0.2.0's image (frame engine off); 231 writes and 11,083,553 with the frame engine on (0.1.0's image, the same code path). TRIG + SCENE: all 16 trigs held and every slot locked in both scenes, 98,681 at most (SCENE A).
conditions.parameterModulation: Not applicable: one apply per press, outside the audio frame. The written values are Part bytes that the stock morph, LFOs and trig locks read as usual.
conditions.modeSwitching: All three modes (SCENE A, SCENE B, both keys), both key orders, one key released from both, scene mutes, and a repeat apply that changes nothing (113,287 instructions). TRIG + SCENE: one scene, the blend, both key orders, the trig released first, a repeat, and stock's gestures inside the chord.
conditions.maxLoad: The worst event is the blend with every enabled slot changing. Executed ColdFire instructions under ot_emu from the YES press to the toast; one instance. Budget: 100 ms of ColdFire time at 266 MHz, a responsiveness target for a key press, not a measured limit.
conditions.inputConditions: Independent of audio and MIDI; runs in the UI task once per press. Executed instructions, not cycles: cache and wait states are not modelled, and time on the unit is not measured.

regions.name: ColdFire code and data (one linked unit, 101 bytes of state)

memory.conditions: The unit as the USB package carries it (2,064 bytes of code and data, no bss; the assembler reports 2,062). No DSP memory, no saved data, no DRAM region of its own.

hardware.summary: On the contributor's Octatrack MKII (OS 1.40C) the USB package of this source (SHA-256 above) was installed with the device tool. On a RAM-booted development twin of main's base the agent drove TRIG + SCENE over USB and read the pattern back: one scene wrote exactly its locks, the blend wrote the morph model's values (XVOL, which has no p-lock, skipped), a repeat showed NOTHING TO LOCK, a trig or knob inside the gesture kept its stock meaning and wrote no p-lock, three trigs at once, the trig released first and a muted scene all wrote, TRIG + PLAY cleared, the live lane took the locks while playing, and removal restored the three sites. Then on the flashed base, beside the user's seven other modules, the user tested by hand: one scene and the blend onto trigs, playback by ear, a project save and a power cycle kept the p-locks, stock gestures inside the chord, TRIG + PLAY.
limitations: One unit, by the contributor and the agent, not an independent reviewer; the MKI was not tested.
USB only: the card build of this source was not flashed.
Nothing timed: how long a TRIG + SCENE or SCENE + YES takes on the unit is not measured; no click or freeze was noticed.
The site's review, Keep and Undo flow was not used: the device tool's try and remove installed and removed it.
MIDI mode, trig pages past the first, pattern and Part changes inside the chord, the arranger and sequencer ACT commit were not tested.
SCENE + YES (unchanged in 0.2.0) was tested on hardware with 0.1.0's package only.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: On a track playing a loop, hold SCENE A and turn FX1's first knob to the left; hold SCENE B and turn it to the right.

Hold SCENE A and press YES. SCENE A APPLIED appears, and FX1's first knob now shows scene A's value. Put the crossfader in the middle, hold SCENE A and SCENE B and press YES: SCENE BLEND APPLIED, and the knob shows the middle value.
Move the crossfader to either end: the sound still reaches each scene's lock. Press FUNC + CUE to reload the Part and the knob returns to where it was.
Press REC, hold a trig, press SCENE A and let go: SCENE A TO TRIGS, and holding the trig shows scene A's value as its p-lock. Hold the trig and press PLAY to clear it again.

access.location: Any audio-track page, with SCENE A, SCENE B or both held; for p-locks, grid recording with trigs held.
steps: Lock parameters in SCENE A and SCENE B as usual (hold the scene key and turn knobs).
Hold SCENE A (or SCENE B) and press YES: that scene's values become the Part's own.
Or move the crossfader to the blend you want, hold SCENE A and SCENE B, and press YES: SCENE BLEND APPLIED.
For p-locks: press REC (grid recording), hold trigs, press SCENE A, SCENE B or both, and let go: SCENE A TO TRIGS, SCENE B TO TRIGS or SCENE BLEND TO TRIGS.
Save the Part to keep the result, or RELOAD PART (FUNC + CUE) to undo.
